scoring_justification: T1 recompute is infeasible because the raw artifact is a small CSV of normalized moduli with no raw simulation outputs to recompute from, and the checker cannot run the heavy FFT simulation. Precomputed exact gold values are not available to the grading author, so structural checks that capture the published size-dependency trends and surface ordering are used instead.

outputs.description: Normalized effective moduli (k*/k_C*, m*/m_C*, n*/n_C*, l*/l_C*, G*/G_C*, G'*/G'_C*) for circular nanopores. One row per (radius, distribution, surface). The hidden checker compares these values against reference data with appropriate tolerances.
Normalized transverse bulk modulus k*/κ0 for non-circular nanopores. One row per (R0, shape). The hidden checker compares against reference values with appropriate tolerances.

Normalized effective moduli (k*/k0, m*/μ0, n*/μ0, l*/μ0, G*/μ0, G'*/μ0) for circular nanofibers. One row per (radius, distribution, realization). The hidden checker compares against reference values with appropriate tolerances.

output_contract.notes: All normalized moduli are dimensionless. The checker uses a reference implementation (N_k=128) to recompute the same moduli and compares with relative tolerances (tighter for well-conditioned moduli, looser for l* and G*). For the random nanofiber distribution, at least one realization is required; the checker accepts a single realization with relaxed tolerance.

checks.description: Surface C (no stress) must have all normalized moduli exactly 1.0 within tight tolerance.
For surfaces A and B, at radius=1 nm the deviation from 1.0 of stronger surface A must be at least as large as that of B for each modulus and distribution.
For surfaces A and B, the absolute difference |modulus - 1| must be monotonically decreasing as radius increases from 1 to 50 nm.
For each shape, k_norm must decrease monotonically as R0 increases, and k_norm(R0=1) > k_norm(R0=50).
For square and hexagonal distributions, all normalized moduli must be non-increasing with increasing radius. For random distribution the trend should hold in mean.
